page: Google Cloud Platform c3-highcpu-176 is an x86_64 compute-oriented instance powered by Intel Xeon 8481C processors running at a base clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The machine provides 176 dedicated vCPUs across 88 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled, paired with 352 GB of system memory at a 2.0 GB per core ratio. Its memory and cache hierarchy comprises 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache per core, and 105 MB of shared L3 cache. It provides hardware support for advanced vector and matrix operations via AVX-512 and Intel AMX, alongside hardware cryptographic instruction sets. This configuration does not include local disk storage or physical GPUs, requiring attached network volumes for persistent file systems.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong multithreaded scalability, placing the multi-core CPU performance within the top tier. Uncached memory read bandwidth measures 458.9 GB/sec, supporting high-throughput parallel execution. Synthetic testing reveals exceptional capacity for request-driven network tasks, achieving 126.23 GB/sec in static web serving throughput and over 164 million operations per second in Redis SET tests. The platform also scores within top brackets for ray tracing and image processing. Conversely, single-threaded processing and archive compression fall into median ranges, indicating that execution performance depends heavily on concurrency and vector parallelization.

From an infrastructure efficiency perspective, the 1:2 core-to-memory balance favors computation-dense tasks over memory-resident caching. The absence of integrated local storage shifts I/O reliance onto external block storage networks. Operational cost efficiency is realized when workloads fully saturate the 176 virtual cores and leverage AMX and AVX-512 optimizations. The server is well configured for large-scale distributed compilation pipelines, static web serving clusters, batch data transformation, and CPU-driven machine learning inference tasks.
